transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood CSM); Evan Lowe (CTO), Marisa Chen (Head of Platform), Jamal Ortiz (SRE), Alisha Patel (Security), Tom Ruiz (Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for making time. quick roll call?
[00:06] Evan: this is Evan, hey everyone.
[00:08] Marisa: Marisa here.
[00:09] Tom: Tom, procurement.
[00:11] Alisha: Alisha, security.
[00:13] Jordan: great, we also have Priya and Marcus on the call from Red— Redwood. so agenda, we want to cover renewal numbers, the UK sovereignty add-on ask, and a capacity top-up for holiday traffic, then go over security Qs. does that sound right?
[00:28] Marisa: yep that's exactly it, thanks.
[00:30] Jordan: cool. quick context—last quarter you ran at about 18k reqs/day with spikes to 28k and you have Dedicated pool D-2 configured with a 2x burst. the renewal we're proposing bumps committed capacity ~35% to handle baseline growth and Q4 burst. Marcus do you want to frame the proposal?
[00:51] Marcus: sure, I can. the proposed term is 12 months, commit increased from 120k token-hours to 160k token-hours monthly equivalent, includes burst for up to 260k for short periods. pricing is similar to current unit rates but with volume discount tiers, and there's an optional UK private VPC add-on priced as a flat monthly infrastructure premium.
[01:18] Evan: can you remind me what's in the UK add-on? is that running Dedicated in a UK region or is it an on-prem? we need to be clear for legal.
[01:27] Priya: yes good question, so the add-on is a customer-managed VPC deployment orchestrated by Redwood Private control plane — you'll get Dedicated GPU pools in the UK region with customer-managed networking and optional bring-your-own-KMS. it's not the on-prem package, it's a VPC-hosted private deployment. apologies if prior notes said otherwise.
[01:46] Alisha: okay so VPC is easier for us, we prefer not to manage hardware. two things — can you confirm KMS integration options and key separation? we need to know if keys are customer-controlled or Redwood-hosted.
[02:00] Priya: we support partner KMS via customer-key-rotation. keys can be customer-managed through our KMS connector or we can integrate with an HSM provider. Redwood keeps an audit trail but cannot decrypt without key access. note: integration modes differ slightly if you pick on-prem.
[02:18] Alisha: audio was a little fuzzy — did you say HSM support?
[02:22] Priya: yes HSM support, sorry.
[02:24] Jamal: for the VPC, what about egress charges and network peering? our cloud team is sensitive to cross-region egress.
[02:32] Marcus: we can estimate egress; for the UK region we typically recommend a direct interconnect or VPC peering. we can send a modelled egress spreadsheet.
[02:41] Tom: procurement will need clear billing language — is the UK add-on monthly invoiced separately?
[02:47] Jordan: yes typically it's a line-item add-on invoiced with monthly committed usage; we can also do an annual prepay if you want to cover the infrastructure premium.
[02:56] Evan: on the capacity top-up — is this purely committed capacity or can we rely on burst? our usage pattern is spiky around promotions.
[03:05] Priya: the trade-off is committed capacity buys lower unit cost and predictable throughput; burst covers short spikes but we can't guarantee sustained throughput beyond the burst window. for sustained increases we recommend committing the delta.
[03:18] Marisa: our internal SLOs are 95th percentile token latency under 200ms for the user-facing endpoints — can Redwood meet that from the UK region?
[03:27] Priya: yes with the Dedicated GPU pools we see median latencies under 120ms for 512-token sequences; 95th can drift with concurrency but with the batch/kv-cache config we can generally target sub-200ms. we'll run a baseline test to validate with your prompt distribution.
[03:41] Evan: okay please run that.
[03:43] Jordan: priya will own the baseline. we'll need a representative prompt set — Marisa, can you share the 200 sample prompts?
[03:50] Marisa: yes I'll drop them in the thread.
[03:53] Priya: great, once we have those we'll run throughput and latency tests across: hosted (eu-west), Dedicated in UK, and fallback hosted path. should take a day of runs.
[04:03] Jamal: are there known mismatches — like quantized model differences in UK vs hosted — that could affect output parity?
[04:11] Priya: slight differences can exist if a model is quantized differently or different kernel selection is used, but we offer a model pinning option to ensure parity; for critical prompts we also recommend an eval set to catch regressions.
[04:23] Alisha: SOC2 and audit questions — we need evidence of controls for the VPC model. does Redwood provide SOC2 attestations and can you include UK-specific data flow diagrams?
[04:34] Marcus: yes we provide SOC2 Type II report; for the private VPC we'll generate a data flow diagram and an audit appendix showing logs, KMS usage, and RBAC mappings. we'll share the compliance pack link after the call.
[04:45] Tom: timeline — we want contract signed before end of December to have capacity in place for January campaigns. is that feasible?
[04:53] Jordan: timeline is tight but feasible. steps: we update quote this week, SE runs baseline next week, security appendix shared, procurement reviews contract terms; if sign-off by 12/20 we can heat up UK region and schedule capacity for early Jan.
[05:07] Tom: will you commit to a provisioning SLA?
[05:10] Jordan: we can include provisioning timelines in the contract — typically 2-4 weeks for UK Dedicated pool once PO is received, expedited options exist for a fee.
[05:19] Evan: I'd like a canary roll out — enable a small percentage of traffic to UK private first and failover to hosted — is that supported?
[05:27] Priya: yes, smart routing can do percent-based rollout and automated fallback to hosted or another model variant. we can show a routing policy config during the pilot.
[05:36] Marisa: any RBAC differences for the private VPC? we need to map our internal roles to Redwood roles.
[05:42] Marcus: we'll provide an RBAC mapping template; in VPC mode you can link SAML/SSO and map groups to roles.
[05:49] Alisha: can you confirm logs retention and whether token-level logs are stored? legal wants minimal PII capture.
[05:56] Priya: by default we store request metadata and token counts for billing; content logs can be disabled for the private deployment or routed to your audit log collector. retention windows are configurable.
[06:06] Evan: good. on pricing — the unit price stepped down in volume tiers; if we move to 24-month term can we get an additional discount?
[06:16] Jordan: yes we can propose a 24-month option with an extra 5% on committed unit rates; we'll put both 12- and 24-month options in the quote.
[06:24] Tom: procurement prefers annual invoicing vs monthly if we prepay. possibilities?
[06:28] Jordan: annual prepay with net-30 invoice is an option, we can structure that.
[06:32] Jamal: Priya, for the latency baseline, what tooling will you use? we use JMeter and a k6 for load but we also have secrets redaction concerns.
[06:41] Priya: we'll run test harness with k6 and Redwood's perf runner. we'll use synthetic traffic and redact any production secrets; results will be a CSV and Grafana dashboard link.
[06:50] Marisa: please include KV cache warmup patterns, since our usage benefits a lot from prefix reuse.
[06:55] Priya: yes we will script prefix-warmup scenarios.
[06:58] Jordan: ok let's walk risks briefly — one is output parity across quantized kernels in region; two is schedule slippage on provisioning; three is egress surprises. mitigation: pin models, provisioning SLA in contract, and egress estimate spreadsheet.
[07:14] Evan: sounds fine.
[07:17] Marcus: I'll post links now: Renewal deck: https://redwood.example/decks/sableworks-renewal-v2.pdf; Compliance pack placeholder: https://redwood.example/compliance/sableworks-pack.zip; Egress model spreadsheet (sample): https://redwood.example/egress/sableworks-estimate.csv
[07:33] Tom: procurement note — contract language around disputed invoices needs clarifying, we'll send markups.
[07:38] Jordan: yes please; send to me and Tom.
[07:42] Alisha: one more security item — do you support SAML single logout? we need end-to-end session termination.
[07:49] Priya: yes SAML SLO supported for the Console, not for API tokens; API tokens are rotated via KMS/HSM.
[07:57] Evan: okay we're roughly in agreement. critical path items for us are the baseline latency test and the contract language for UK data flows.
[08:07] Jordan: agreed. quick timing recap: Jordan sends updated quote (with 12/24 month options and UK add-on) by 11/24; Priya runs tests and posts results by 11/25; Marcus shares runbook by 11/22; Alisha posts required controls list by 11/26; Evan to confirm sign-off timeline by 11/30.
[08:28] Marisa: will there be any changes to the SLA numbers with the add-on? specifically latency SLOs?
[08:33] Jordan: the SLA terms remain, but we can append a regional latency target in the schedule as a best-effort SLO and include remediation steps if targets are missed. procurement any objection?
[08:45] Tom: need legal to review but seems acceptable if it's not a punitive SLA.
[08:50] Jordan: understood.
[08:52] Evan: anything else?
[08:54] Jamal: one operational ask — can we get a runbook for failover steps if UK region experiences degraded performance?
[08:59] Marcus: yes we'll add a runbook with routing flip instructions and recommended traffic percentages for canary.
[09:05] Jordan: ok final quick: we'll follow up with three artifacts: updated quote, perf results, compliance pack. after those you can route to legal/procurement and we can schedule a contract review meeting.
[09:18] Marisa: thanks everyone.
[09:20] Tom: thanks.
[09:22] Alisha: thanks.
[09:24] Jordan: thanks all. end call.

Notes on transcription: occasional label jitter; some technical terms transcribed phonetically (e.g., "Detticated" for Dedicated). Action items and links captured above.
